Add `parse_amount(text)` to `ledgerly/importers.py` that turns such text into an amount: ignore surrounding whitespace, an optional leading `$` and thousands separators. Reject text that is not a valid non-negative amount with at most two decimal places.

## Notes from earlier work
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0008] Parse rates via Decimal(str(...)): Parse numeric rate inputs with `Decimal(str(rate_percent))` and reject bools and non-finite values before range checks, so floats and strings are handled consistently.
  (learned from task E05 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0002] Raise BillingError with snake_case code and string detail: Reject invalid input by raising BillingError(code, detail) from ledgerly.errors with a snake_case code (e.g. "invalid_state", "negative_amount") and a str()/repr() of the offending value as detail, matching payments.py and invoice.py.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 3x, 2 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0007] Refunds above 500.00 need approved_by: Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver per finance policy FIN-2026-03: accept keyword-only `approved_by=None` and raise `BillingError("approval_required")` when the amount exceeds the threshold and no approver is given. Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source FIN-2026-03; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0001] Normalize unit_price with to_money before storing: In ledgerly/invoice.py, convert any incoming price with to_money() from ledgerly.money before constructing a LineItem, so unit_price is always a Decimal; compare against ZERO for sign checks.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0003] Exclude bool when validating integer quantities: When validating integer arguments in ledgerly, guard with isinstance(x, bool) first because bool is a subclass of int; reject True/False explicitly before the int check.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 1 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0009] Record state changes via audit.record: Every payment/invoice state change must emit an audit event through ledgerly.audit.record with a snake_case event name and the entity id plus amount.
  (learned from task E06 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
